markingDesign.vocabulary: TW-9's, extended rather than duplicated. resolution / proxy_of / proxy_note are the exact keys apps/cockpit/backend/app/data/futures_catalog.json already uses for borrowed CFTC series, kept snake_case in TypeScript on purpose so one `grep proxy_of` finds every marked proxy in the repo, frontend and backend alike.
markingDesign.newEnumValue: tracking-fund-proxy, joining exact and parent-contract-proxy. A listed fund standing in for a contract is a different KIND of borrow from a parent contract standing in for its micro, so it earns a value, not a second field set.
markingDesign.provenanceAdded: each of the 41 entries states that the numbers are FMP's for the fund via GET /fundamentals/{fund}/panel, and that the root-to-fund mapping itself is a hand-curated operator table that no exchange or vendor publishes.
markingDesign.perEntryNote: names BOTH the fund and the contract it stands in for, plus a per-fund structural caveat (trust vs contract, index basket, roll behaviour). /CL->USO says the roll is the hazard and calls itself the sharpest case in the table rather than the safest.
markingDesign.structuralGuarantee: futuresFundamentalsProxy returns FundamentalsProxy | null instead of string | null, so the substituted ticker is unreachable without its marker. The UI half is a component with no unmarked variant and no suppression prop.
markingDesign.sharedHelper: proxyMark lives in apps/empressa/frontend/src/utils/proxyMark.ts, the tree both the cockpit web app and the mobile app alias as @empressa, so the two Trade Grids cannot drift into different answers about one borrow — and one CI-gated test pins the marker both render.

ciGapClosed.finding: CI ran ZERO frontend assertions. The workflow ran pytest, `vite build` and gitleaks. `vite build` proves the bundle compiles and asserts nothing, so a frontend contract could be deleted and main would stay green — which is exactly how a backend-sealed proxy marker could be dropped by two UIs with nothing red.
ciGapClosed.fix: added a test-frontend job running the existing, previously ungated vitest suite. vite.config.ts already includes ../../empressa/frontend/src/**, so the frozen @empressa components that ship inside the live cockpit bundle are now gated too.
ciGapClosed.beforeAfter: baseline 35 files / 421 tests (already green, no pre-existing failures repaired or suppressed); now 39 files / 446 tests.

doNotWeakenCheck: every TW-9 artifact is byte-identical to main on this branch — futures_catalog.json, providers/cftc.py, providers/futures_reference.py, adaptive_panel.py, tests/test_signal_heatmap.py, bots/presets.py all verified UNCHANGED via git diff --quiet against origin/main.
remaining: The mobile render path has no test runner — apps/cockpit/mobile has no `test` script and no vitest. CI pins the shared proxyMark that screen consumes, and the mobile build was run locally and verified to contain the marker strings, but the mobile JSX itself is not asserted. Closing this means adding vitest to the mobile package and a CI job for it.

apps/cockpit/backend/app/bots/presets.py::weekly_proxy() still returns a bare string. Its only serving consumer marks the result and that is pinned by existing tests, so this is latent rather than live — but the same structural hardening applied to the frontend lookup (return the marked record, not the ticker) would close it. empressa-mobile.vercel.app is serving the cockpit web build rather than the mobile build. That is a deploy-wiring fact discovered while establishing deployedSurfaces, not a TW-12 defect, and it is unowned — worth an operator call on whether the mobile project is intended to be live.

apps/empressa has its own vitest.config.ts whose include glob is `frontend/src/**/*.test.ts` — .ts only, so it would not pick up the .tsx test added here. Harmless today because nothing runs that config in CI, but it is a naming inconsistency between the two configs.
